title: Investigate sub-second burst metering that caused customer quota overage appeal
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Customer reported an apparent unexplained quota overage for a monthly quota despite traffic patterns that should have stayed well under threshold. Root cause needed to determine whether this was a billing/metering bug, instrumentation double-counting, or an integration producing micro-bursts that we failed to aggregate correctly.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer webhook integration sends ~60 requests per second in 1-2 request bursts from multiple regional edge IPs
2) Each request is <200 tokens; requests are spread across many short-lived HTTP connections

3) Our ingestion pipeline recorded tokens but our burst-window aggregation used a 1-second window with a race between front proxy and ingestion that could double-count when requests crossed node boundaries
4) Replayed similar traffic on staging with distributed proxies reproduced the inflated token counts reported in production logs
impact_summary: One enterprise customer (Acme Health) received an unexpected overage invoice and opened a formal dispute. Immediate business risk: churn and loss of trust. Technical risk: flaw in burst aggregation could affect other customers using webhook-style integrations.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-23: Support escalated ticket from Acme Health; initial invoice ID INV-2026-02-119 attached in docs
2026-02-24: Correlated customer timestamps with ingestion logs; noticed token counts aligned with request 'start' events but missing de-duplication when requests forwarded across proxy pool
2026-02-25: Replayed a representative traffic pattern in staging using loadgen script (scripts/replay/burst-replay.py) and observed ~1.9x token counts compared to expected accounting

2026-02-26: Identified race condition in burst window aggregator: aggregator keyed by connection_id when it should be keyed by request_id + upstream_node; concurrent writes occasionally caused the aggregator to process the same logical token span twice
2026-03-01: Drafted fix to aggregator to use deterministic request fingerprinting and atomic increment via redis HINCRBY with optimistic locking (PR in linked_prs)
2026-03-03: Added end-to-end test coverage (unit + integration) and a new metering regression test in ci/metering-regress.yml
2026-03-04: Performed backfill simulation for affected date range and reconciled expected vs billed; prepared credit calculation
2026-03-06: Support authorized a partial credit pending legal approval; Finance confirmed credit amount and invoice reversal process
2026-03-09: Credit issued to Acme Health and confirmation received; support closed the dispute with the customer
root_cause_summary: A race condition in the burst-window aggregation logic caused sub-second, multi-node bursts to be double-counted. The aggregator used a non-unique connection key leading to concurrent increments for the same logical token span when requests crossed proxy boundaries
resolution: Merged fix to deterministic request fingerprinting and atomic increments: runtime PR #3456
Deployed hotfix to production (canary -> global) on 2026-03-03 under release billing-2026.03
Backfilled corrected counts for all affected accounts and computed credits
Issued $12,400 credit to Acme Health (INV-2026-02-119) on 2026-03-09 and sent reimbursement confirmation
Added metering regression tests to CI and an alert to billing-monitoring for token count deltas > 15% between ingestion and aggregator
Documented incident and postmortem; recommended long-term plan to simplify aggregator keying and move to single-writer per-fingerprint model
